catalog_quote: 1.4 Stress. Stress in Matigsalug always occurs on the second-to-last (penultimate) vowel when a word occurs in isolation. Because it is predictable, stress is not marked on written texts. On words ending with a long vowel, the rule still applies. The long vowel is written as two consecutive vowels, and the stress falls on the second-to-last one so, in essence, the stress falls on the long vowel. Matigsalug does have small one-syllable particles and pronouns that act as clitics, phonologically joining to the previous word thus causing the stress to move to the last vowel of the previous word (which is now the penultimate vowel of the combined unit). ámey 'father' / améy rin 'his father'. However, in this document, as in normal Matigsalug writing, stress is not marked. ... [sec. 1.2] Geminate vowels occur in Matigsalug, although with a relatively low frequency. sweep_summary: The one works with stress in the title, Meiklejohn & Meiklejohn 1958 'Accentuation in Sarangani Manobo' (OLM 3, pp. 1-3), is about Sarangani Manobo (ISO mbs, sara1327), a different Manobo language; Glottolog links it to mati1250 only via WALS's mis-sourced lect 'Kulamanen' (kuz), whose 14A/15A/17A values derive from it and Dubois 1976. It is print-only (no copy on archive.org, SIL, HathiTrust or Google Books reachable; Re-read first-hand: the catalog's deciding source Wang et al. 2006 sec. 1.4 (Internet Archive copy 20100616, saved) matches the catalog quote verbatim (predictable penultimate-vowel stress, final long vowel stressed, enclitic/suffix shift) -> confirms. Also read and page-verified Strong 1979 (Tigwa Manobo, SIPL 3(1):165-178, held by the project): predictable, non-phonemic stress, penultimate except antepenult in trisyllables, secondary stress two syllables left -> refines (Tigwa-specific detail, no weight clause; contradicts the WALS Kulamanen coding). Weight coding stands; the Tigwa statement does not supersede Wang et al. 2006. Still unreached (paywalled/print): Wang 1991 PJL 22:1-29 and McGriff 1995 PJL 26:33-42, the detailed Matigsalug phonologies cited by the grammar.

new_statements.quote: Stress in Tigwa Manobo is predictable. Primary stress (´) falls normally on the penultimate syllable, except that on 3-syllable words it falls on the antepenult. Secondary stress (`) falls normally on the third syllable before the primary stress, except that in 4-syllable words it falls on the first syllable. 2-syllable /qúg.pit/ 'bolo'; 3-syllable /bá.ka.ka/ 'kingfisher'; 4-syllable /bì.goq.bí.goq/ (species of eel); 6-syllable /qog.pà.ka.ti.núg.puq/ 'jump'.

new_statements.reading: First-hand SIL phonology of the Tigwa lect (ISO mbt): stress is predictable and non-phonemic, penultimate by default with an antepenultimate exception in trisyllables, secondary stress two syllables to the left (word-initial in 4-syllable words); no weight or vowel-quality conditioning. It corroborates the catalog's 'predictable, penultimate' core for the mbt cluster and refutes the WALS/StressTyp2 'Kulamanen' (Sarangani-sourced) coding, but it describes Tigwa, which Wang et al. 2006 treat as a closely related language, and it lacks the final-long-vowel clause that drives the catalog's weight coding.

audit.recode_to: Only if Wang 1991/McGriff 1995 syllabify VV as two syllables (as Strong 1979 does for the Tigwa dialect): reclassify from 'weight (CVV, right edge)' to quantity-insensitive fixed penultimate (syllable = vowel), keeping the clitic-group domain note. no reclassification on present evidence.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation, the sec. 1.2 geminate-vowel sentence and fn. 38 are all verbatim in the SIL PDF we hold of Wang et al. 2006 at the stated places. (2) Deciding source: a 2006 SIL reference grammar (Glottolog's only grammar for the languoid), publisher text, independently verified — authoritative for the rule 'stress on the penultimate vowel'. The weak point is not the source but the inference: the grammar never calls VV a heavy syllable; it counts vowels ('penultimate vowel'; long vowel written and counted as two vowels; fn. 38 'penultimate syllable'). The 'weight/CVV' label is our extensional reading of 'in essence, the stress falls on the long vowel'. sources.note: Tigwa Manobo is coded under ISO mbt / mati1250 (Ethnologue dialect) but Wang et al. 2006 (Introduction, p. ix) call it a closely related language rather than a Matigsalug dialect. Strong gives predictable, non-phonemic stress: penultimate syllable by default, antepenult in trisyllables, with secondary stress two syllables before the primary (initial in 4-syllable words); no vowel-quality or schwa condition, no weight condition.
